title: SylphCloud Systems — integration & channel discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery: SylphCloud exploring a channel integration with Redwood for a hosted + private hybrid offering. Discussed technical constraints (multi-tenant GPU pools, VPC peering, certs), go-to-market mechanics, and next steps to run a short perf benchmark and draft a partner integration checklist.
topics: commercial routing and revenue share mechanics
action_items: Alexei: Share Redwood partner one-pager and integration checklist (by 2028-04-24)
Priya: Provide example infra diagram and suggested endpoint configs (by 2028-04-26)
Maya: Confirm SylphCloud's compliance checklist and primary legal contact (by 2028-04-25)
Leena: Provide sample workload with 95th percentile latency target and dataset access for benchmark (by 2028-05-02)
next_steps: Schedule a technical deep dive for infra alignment (SE-led)
Exchange partner integration docs and security questionnaire
Plan 2-week pilot: 3 workloads, one dedicated GPU pool + one hosted fallback
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-22 UTC 15:00 — Duration 48m
Attendees: Alexei (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood SE); Maya (SylphCloud Head of Platform), Rafael (Partnerships), Leena (Cloud Architect), Tom (SRE)

[00:00] Alexei: Hey everyone thanks for joining, excited to learn more about SylphCloud and how you two think about partnering on GPU and cloud onramp. Quick round-robin?
[00:12] Maya: Hi all, Maya here. We run SylphCloud, we provide a managed multi-tenant cloud for AI workloads, we also do channel deals with resellers. Rafael will lead biz ops.
[00:20] Rafael: yeah hi, thanks for making time. We're looking at partners who can give a production-grade inference runtime we can bundle.
[00:28] Priya: Great. One thing up front, are you primarily targeting marketplace listing or a deeper reseller/integration where you host Redwood nodes inside SylphCloud?
[00:38] Leena: Good question. We want both options. Marketplace for quick onboarding, but we have some enterprise customers that require VPC peering and private deployments so deeper integration is important.
[00:49] Daniel: Understood — that aligns with what Redwood offers hosted + dedicated + private. Curious on your expected scale and GPU types?
[00:57] Tom: We're backing the stack with A100s today, moving some customers to H100. For multi-tenant we use Kubernetes with SR-IOV and custom device plugins. Our latency SLAs are 50–150ms 95p for many customers, though a few high-frequency apps want 20–40ms.
[01:18] Priya: 20–40ms is pretty tight — that's usually Dedicated or on-prem with pinned capacity. For hosted we have fast response profiles but tail latencies depend on batch settings and network hops. Have you measured end-to-end from your edge?
[01:32] Leena: We have internal tests but not for a Redwood runtime. We'd like to run a small benchmark to understand the tradeoffs.
[01:39] Alexei: Totally — typically we pilot with two workloads: one latency-sensitive low-token-rate chat, and one higher-throughput embedding batch. We'll provide an example harness.
[01:49] Rafael: Commercially, we're thinking revenue share for marketplace listing, but a different margin if we host private clusters on SylphCloud. How flexible are your routing and billing APIs?
[02:01] Alexei: We expose per-token usage, model routes, and can route by policy (latency first vs cost first). Billing can be pulled via usage exports and webhooks. For reseller deals we support metering and attribution so you can bill customers directly.
[02:14] Maya: Security is a big one. We need SOC2 docs, KMS integration, and proof of audit logs. Also SSO/SAML for partner portals.
[02:24] Priya: We have SOC 2 Type II and an enterprise compliance pack. KMS integrations include AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or Cloud Storage. We'll share security docs after the call.
[02:39] Tom: For private deployments, do you support air-gapped installs or do you require a control plane egress? Some regulated customers need zero egress.
[02:49] Daniel: We have two private deployment modes: a customer-managed control plane with optional offline (air-gapped) package. The tradeoff is with telemetry and automated rollouts; offline installs require manual upgrades.
[03:02] Leena: Okay that sounds promising. On the infra side, would Redwood's runtime play nicely with our existing device plugin and our KV cache abstractions?
[03:11] Priya: Our runtime has an abstraction layer for device management; we can adapt to common plugins. KV cache — we support both local GPU KV cache and remote prefix caching. We might need a short integration spike to confirm your APIs align.
[03:25] Rafael: How long is a typical integration for deeper private deployment? Weeks? Months?
[03:30] Alexei: For a pilot where Redwood runs in your environment with one dedicated pool, typical is 4–8 weeks: infra alignment, security review, pilot run, then performance tuning. Marketplace listings can be much faster — days to weeks depending on legal.
[03:43] Maya: What about model onboarding? Customers use a mix of open models and some proprietary ones. We need model controls and ability to pin versions.
[03:51] Daniel: We support model cataloging, version pinning, and automatic fallbacks to quantized variants. For proprietary models you can either host them on your private deployment or provide them to a Redwood private instance under NDA.
[04:04] Leena: We also need to know about observability. Our SREs like per-token breakdown, traces, and request-level latency.
[04:12] Priya: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We can also forward metrics to Prometheus/Grafana in your cluster.
[04:21] Tom: Noise in transcription: sorry, that was me.
[04:24] (laughter)
[04:26] [04:26] Rafael: A couple of red flags we've seen with other vendors: opaque pricing and vendor lock-in on model variants. How do you handle quantization and runtime differences?
[04:36] Alexei: We try to be transparent — we publish performance profiles across hardware and quant levels. Lock-in is minimized by letting customers pin model versions and export logs/metrics. We'll share our quantization compatibility matrix.
[04:46] Leena: For the benchmark, what endpoints will you need from us? Network egress, sample corpora?
[04:53] Priya: Minimum: a VPC peering/VPN for private pilot, sample dataset (anonymized), latency target, and expected QPS. We'll run 2–3 days of synthetic and 3–5 days of production-mirrored traffic if you can provide it.
[05:07] Maya: On commercial mechanics: we want co-marketing, joint case study, and clear support SLAs for partner customers.
[05:15] Alexei: Absolutely — we typically do a partner launch playbook that includes a joint case study, co-branded collateral, and a support handoff model. I'll include that in the one-pager.
[05:24] Rafael: Any blockers on our side to start a pilot?
[05:28] Priya: Mostly legal + security questionnaire, and your infra contact for peering. Tech-wise we just need the access details and a small test cluster for initial runs.
[05:38] Leena: We'll compile the questionnaire and pick the workloads.
[05:42] Alexei: Great. I'll send the partner docs. One technical note: if you want 20–40ms 95p for chat, we'll recommend dedicated pools with low batch windows and co-located inference to your VPC — that may increase cost but hit the targets.
[05:58] Tom: Makes sense. Do you support mixed-precision or INT8 for some models to reduce cost?
[06:04] Daniel: Yes, mixed-precision and INT8 quantized routes are supported; we can suggest model-quality profiles so we can recommend tradeoffs between cost and accuracy.
[06:15] Priya: Also worth noting: our smart routing can fall back to hosted cheaper variants if your dedicated pool is saturated, so customer apps stay online. That might be useful for peak events.
[06:27] Maya: That is attractive. For the marketplace listing, do you expose APIs for onboarding customers self-serve?
[06:33] Alexei: Yes, marketplace flow supports self-serve sign-up, with optional verification steps for enterprise. You can also gate features behind reseller agreements.
[06:41] Rafael: Alright next steps recap?
[06:44] Alexei: I'll send the partner one-pager, integration checklist, and security pack by Tuesday (2028-04-24). Priya will prepare an infra diagram and endpoint template. You (Maya/Leena) will share workloads and compliance contacts. We'll schedule a SE deep dive next week to go over the benchmark plan.
[07:02] Leena: Sounds good. One last question: any restrictions on model licensing for marketplace customers?
[07:09] Daniel: We can support most open models; proprietary licensed models need a license agreement. We'll surface those in the integration docs.
[07:17] Maya: Thanks everyone, this was useful. We'll follow up in the thread.
[07:21] Alexei: Thanks — talk soon.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription noise: some proper nouns like SR-IOV, H100, and model names may be mis-transcribed in places.
